restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; fresh independent uniform 256-bit words, not seeded PRNG expansion.
Exactly 32-byte messages msg(x)=BE32(x), one 64-byte padded block per hash; complete SHA-256 with fixed IV, prefix rounds 0 through 31, feed-forward and all 256 digest bits.
Single-processor van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point search with theta=2^-32, chain cap L=2^40, budget K0=65300*2^112 evaluations and record cap 2^98; one finite run, no restarts.
One finite run with at most 2^128.02 target-compression equivalents of total charged computation and at most 2^112 peak bytes; no nonuniform advice or precomputed collision.
Analytic resource and success bounds under score-critical heuristic H-RF; no full-scale execution, cryptanalytic weakness or nominal-reference improvement is claimed.

heuristics.statement: Each evaluation of the 32-round SHA-256 ordinary-collision map f at a fresh input returns a value uniform on {0,1}^256, independent of all previous coins and outputs.
heuristics.scope: Used only for the success-probability bound of the distinguished-point walk (first-contact and bad-event estimates). Correctness and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds hold for every run without this premise.
heuristics.extrapolation: From standard generic-search modeling to the fixed 32-round prefix target; no differential, independence-across-rounds or balance premise about SHA-256 structure is assumed beyond generic random-function behavior for contact statistics.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is a modeling heuristic, not a proved property of the fixed function. Supporting discussion is analytic (birthday contact arithmetic plus standard DP literature); no organizer-executed scaled experiment is declared. The claimed margin above 0.39 is about 0.0012 before deducting bad events below 2.4e-10. A shortfall in contact rate would require a larger budget at about 2.4 times the shortfall in bits.
